description: Operator-read follower joint angles at two reference poses. Read-only observations of /joint_states; the servo zero was not changed. Used as the starting reference for the sim visual offsets and for the limits review, not as a calibration.
method: Operator placed the arm by hand at each pose with the driver running; the console host read /joint_states three times one second apart and all three readings agreed to 0.01 deg. Angles in degrees, gripper in metres, as published by the driver.

vendor_standby_reference.what: The vendor's standby posture from the Alicia-D installation guide: every joint at its zero, joint protrusions and camera-post protrusion pointing diagonally upward, placed by eye.
vendor_standby_reference.placement_confidence: Operator placed the pose by eye twice. The first placement read Joint3 at -4.04 and Joint5 at 1.49; the operator judged the Joint3 placement poor, re-placed the arm, and the second placement (recorded here) read Joint3 at -0.97. Placement repeatability by eye is therefore about 3 deg on Joint3 and under 0.5 deg elsewhere.

folded_rest.what: The folded rest position the arm is left in between sessions; the pose every take started or ended in on 2026-10-17.

notes: read_minus_model_deg is the encoder reading at the vendor reference pose; the implied per-joint correction for a model-true display is its negative. The reference pose is itself placed by eye, so these are starting values, not measured zero offsets.

At the reference pose every joint reads within 2 deg of the model zero, so the -4.0 deg Joint2 visual offset the Isaac record mode uses (chosen by eye on 2026-10-17 with the real gripper touching the table) is not a zero mismatch. It is the pose-dependent gravity sag and gear play under load at the table, which a constant offset only approximates.

Folded rest exceeds the configured Joint2 recording bound of 96 deg and sits 0.5 deg inside the Joint3 lower bound of -34 deg (config/synria_limits.yaml), which is why takes that start or end at rest fail the limits gate.
Gravity sag and gear play are not separated here; they need the from-above and from-below readings described in the operator runbook.
